ocs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/list-a-suites-eval-cases.md): Every case in the suite, in the public steps-first shape.\n-
[Create an eval case](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/create-an-eval-case.md): Adds one case to the suite. Both `t
itle` and a non-empty `steps` array are required — `steps` is optional on the shared case shape so PATCH can be partial, but a cas
e persisted without executable steps could never run. When `models` is omitted the suite's configured model is used.\n- [Create se
veral eval cases](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/create-several-eval-cases.md): Adds up to 100 cases to the suite
in one call — the bulk form of the single create, and the way to import a suite or convert a repo's test files without a round tr
ip per case. Every entry needs a `title` and a non-empty `steps` array. Cases are validated together and reported individually: a
`failed…\n- [Generate eval cases from the suite's tools](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/generate-eval-cases-from-
the-suites-tools.md): Discovers the suite's server tools over a live MCP connection, generates cases against them, and persists th
em — the only edit route that connects to a server. Synchronous: connect, generate, persist, disconnect, respond.\n- [Author eval
cases from a document](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/author-eval-cases-from-a-document.md): The sibling of `case
s/generate`: generation invents cases from the suite's tools, import reads them out of something a person already wrote — a test p
lan, a spreadsheet of scenarios, a JSON export. MCPJam's own model turns the document into full cases (ordered steps, tool calls,
assertions), so the…\n- [Read an eval authoring job](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/read-an-eval-authoring-job.md
): Progress and drafts for a job started by `cases/generate` or `cases/import`. Poll this after a `202`, then commit the job once
its `status` is `completed`.\n- [Write a finished authoring job's cases into the suite](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval
-runs/write-a-finished-authoring-jobs-cases-into-the-suite.md): Writes the job's drafts into the suite. A draft carrying unresolve
d blocking issues or proposed additions is **skipped** rather than written, and comes back under `skipped` with a `reviewUrl` for
finishing it in the app.\n- [Get one eval case](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/get-one-eval-case.md): A case that
belongs to this suite and project. A case in another suite is a 404, not a 403.\n- [Delete an eval case](https://docs.mcpjam.com/
api-reference/eval-runs/delete-an-eval-case.md): Removes the case from the suite. Past runs that executed it are not affected.\n-
[Update an eval case](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/update-an-eval-case.md): Partial update — omitted fields are
left as they are. Supplying `steps` REPLACES the case's definition rather than merging into it. `matchOptions` and `checks` accep
t `null` to clear the case-level override and fall back to the suite's.\n- [Upload a run artifact](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-ref
erence/eval-runs/upload-a-run-artifact.md): Stores one artifact referenced by an ingested run (typically widget HTML too large to
send inline) and returns the `storageId` the run's results then reference. This is what `reportEvalResults` in `@mcpjam/sdk` uses
for widget evidence.\n- [Get an upload URL for a run artifact](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/get-an-upload-url-f
or-a-run-artifact.md): Retired. Every request answers `410 Gone` with `code: \"FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED\"` and `details.code: \"SDK_U
PGRADE_REQUIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload a run artifact by sending its bytes to `POST /projects/{projectId}/eval-
ingest/artifacts`, which returns the `storageId` the run's results…\n- [Discover authenticated eval ingestion capabilities](https:
//docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/discover-authenticated-eval-ingestion-capabilities.md): Discover authenticated eval inge
stion capabilities. Uses the SDK reporting transport and the same tenant/project authorization as eval ingestion. Unsupported capa
bilities remain absent.\n- [Persist advisory case-run evaluations](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/persist-advisor
y-case-run-evaluations.md): Persist advisory case-run evaluations. Uses the SDK reporting transport and the same tenant/project au
thorization as eval ingestion. Unsupported capabilities remain absent.\n- [Ingest a completed eval run in one call](https://docs.m
cpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/ingest-a-completed-eval-run-in-one-call.md): The whole-run variant: submit a finished run and it
s iterations in a single request. This is what the SDK reporter uses by default.\n- [Mint a model lease for MCPJam-hosted inferenc
e](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/mint-a-model-lease-for-mcpjam-hosted-inference.md): How an SDK eval running OUT
SIDE the platform (local dev, CI) uses MCPJam-hosted inference on the organization's credits, with no provider key of its own. Aut
henticate like any other `/api/v1` route (typically an `sk_` key).\n- [Revoke a model lease](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference
/eval-runs/revoke-a-model-lease.md): Kills this caller's SDK model leases under `runId` in the addressed project, immediately — th
e proxy fails a revoked lease closed from that moment. Leases also expire on their own, so this is for ending a run early (an SDK
suite calls it at teardown) rather than something a caller must do.\n- [Close an open ingestion run](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-r
eference/eval-runs/close-an-open-ingestion-run.md): Marks the run complete and computes its rollups. Until this is called the run
stays open in the dashboard.\n- [Append iterations to an open run](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/append-iteratio
ns-to-an-open-run.md): Appends one batch of iteration results to a run opened by `runs/start`.\n- [Authenticate and record an eval
start](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/authenticate-and-record-an-eval-start.md): Called by official SDK, CLI and
Vitest runners before executing an eval. Requires an organization API key or saved-login bearer. Records only start metadata, cre
ates no dashboard run, and applies no debit or quota draw. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage. Reuse the runStartI
d for ret…\n- [Open a run for incremental ingestion](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/open-a-run-for-incremental-in
gestion.md): Opens a run that iterations are appended to, for a long CI job that reports as it goes. Pair with `runs/iterations` a
nd `runs/finalize`.\n- [Get a run's gate waiver](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/get-a-runs-gate-waiver.md): The w
aiver in force over this run, or `null`. Available to anyone who can VIEW the run, not only to those who can grant one — a waiver
its readers cannot see is not a visible waiver.\n- [Waive a run gate](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/waive-a-run-
gate.md): Override a FAILING run's release gate until an expiry you name. This does NOT make the run pass: the run keeps its `resu
lt`, the waiver is a separate audited record, and every surface that honors it — the GitHub Check Run and the CLI's `eval gate` —
reports the gate as waived, by whom, why, and unti…\n- [Revoke a gate waiver](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/revo
ke-a-gate-waiver.md): End a waiver early, putting the gate and the GitHub Check Run back. Requires the manage tier.\n- [Preview de
terministic draft evaluators against stored evidence](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/preview-deterministic-draft-
evaluators-against-stored-evidence.md): Requires suite configuration permission and a terminal run. Reserves a 60-second determini
stic-preview cooldown, independent of judge previews. Supply the returned continuation object with the unchanged draft to read the
next bounded population. Reads at most 100 iterations within a 30-second operat…\n- [Read the organization's spend budget](https:
//docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/read-the-organizations-spend-budget.md): The ceiling on what this organization may spend o
n MCPJam-billed work — chat, evals, judges and computer time — in the current billing window, and how much of it has been spent.\n
